newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's ex-P2 leader Gelli released after arrest.
newsitem.headline: Italy's ex-P2 leader Gelli released after arrest.

text.p: Licio Gelli, the former grandmaster of the outlawed P2 masonic lodge, was arrested in central Italy on Thursday but released within hours after magistrates said there had been a misunderstanding.

Gelli, whose lodge was at the centre of a political conspiracy scandal that brought down a government in 1981, was arrested at his home in the Tuscan city of Arezzo and taken to local police headquarters.

Magistrates in Rome, who had ordered the arrest, later acknowledged that the terms of his extradition to Italy from Switzerland more than a decade ago meant the 75-year-old could not be made to serve a jail term.
"The arrest order has been revoked," a judicial source said. Italian news agencies reported from Arezzo that Gelli had left the police building without comment six hours after his arrest.
Gelli has three years of a prison sentence pending after the conclusion of a final appeal in a long-running trial into the alleged illegal workings of P2, or Propaganda Due.
Gelli's lawyer, Michele Gentiloni, asked for the immediate suspension of the warrant on the grounds that his client was not liable to serve the sentence under the terms of his extradition.
Gelli was arrested in 1983 in Switzerland, which conceded his extradition on condition that he would not be tried on perceived "political' charges.

The Court of Cassation, Italy's highest court, confirmed an eight-year jail sentence on Gelli last November for illegal procurement of confidential documents. Five years of the sentence were suspended, leaving Gelli to serve three.

The P2 lodge came to light in 1981 during an enquiry into banker Roberto Calvi, a lodge member who was found hanged in London the following year shortly before the spectacular collapse of his Banco Ambrosiano bank.

The lodge was found to have some 1,000 prominent members including top politicians, businessmen and military officers and its exposure brought down the Christian Democrat-led government of Arnaldo Forlani.

Investigations into P2 activities have repeatedly delved into allegations that the lodge conspired with right-wing extremists and the Mafia to destabilise the state through bombings and other acts of violence.
Conflicting findings by courts and parliamentary enquiries, however, have failed to resolve the case.
